title: Integrated Finance & Legal Playbook: Budgeting, Forecasting, Contracts, Procurement, RevRec & Billing
author: Avery Chen
content:
Summary:
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's core Finance and Legal operating procedures for annual budgeting and rolling forecasting, contracts and legal review, procurement approvals and vendor onboarding, and revenue recognition (RevRec) and billing operations. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and business owners who participate in planning, contracting, and revenue processes.

Scope and purpose:
- Scope: applies to all Redwood legal entities and business units. Includes hosted API, Dedicated, and Private product revenue and contractual commitments.
- Purpose: reduce cycle time for approvals, ensure consistent RevRec treatment, centralize procurement controls, and minimize revenue leakage.

Ownership and roles:
- Finance: owns budgeting and forecasting process, RevRec model, and billing cadence. Responsible: Director of Finance (primary contact: Avery Chen).
- Legal: owns contract language standards, SLAs, indemnities, and signatory authority. Responsible: GC (primary contact: Maya Singh).
- Procurement/Procure-to-Pay (P2P): owns vendor onboarding, PO issuance, and payment terms. Responsible: Procurement Lead (Kyle Brooks).
- Business owners/Product/GT M: own inputs to forecasts, contract commercial terms, and acceptance criteria for vendor deliverables.

Key definitions:
- Budget: annual resource and spend plan approved by Finance & the Executive Team.
- Rolling Forecast: 12-month forward-looking revenue & expense plan updated at least monthly.
- RevRec: revenue recognition policy aligned to ASC 606 principles (performance obligations, transaction price allocation, timing of recognition).
- PO: purchase order issued to commit spend.

Annual budgeting and rolling forecast process:
1. Timeline (typical):
   1. Q3 (July–September): Strategic planning and initial headcount requests.
   2. October: Finance issues Budget Template and planning guidance.
   3. November: Department submissions due.
   4. December: Finance consolidates and Exec review. Board packet prepared for January meeting.
2. Inputs required from teams:
   - Revenue build by product/route (USD monthly cadence).
   - Headcount plan by role & expected hire date.
   - Major capital expenditures (servers, on-prem packaging costs).
   - Dedicated/partner contract renewal assumptions.
3. Approval gates:
   - Department lead -> Finance review -> CFO approval -> Exec sign-off -> Board (if material change >10% of ARR projection).
4. Rolling forecast cadence:
   - Monthly submission of updated revenue and expense by product. Finance consolidates and publishes variance vs. budget.

Forecasting controls and model specifics:
- Use the canonical Finance forecast workbook in the Finance Drive (link internal).
- Assumptions must include conversion rates for self-serve signups, average revenue per user (ARPU) by tier, churn assumptions, and committed vs usage-based revenue split.
- Sensitivity scenarios: Base / Upside (+15%) / Downside (-15%).

Contract review and legal process:
1. Standard contract types covered:
   - Standard SaaS license / API agreement (hosted inference).
   - Dedicated capacity / Reserved capacity contracts.
   - Private deployment / On-prem license and service agreements.
   - Master Subscription Agreement (MSA) + SOWs.
2. Contract lifecycle steps:
   1. Request commercial term via Sales/AE and attach template order form.
   2. Legal performs risk assessment and redline using the internal clause library.
   3. Finance verifies pricing, RevRec accounting treatment, and billing cadence.
   4. Procurement/Vendor Management (if third party involved) performs vendor diligence.
   5. Exec signatory approval if outside delegation.
3. Approval matrix (signatory authority):
   | Approval Level | Annual Contract Value (ACV) | Required Approvals |
   |----------------|---------------------------:|--------------------|
   | Team Lead      | <= $50k                   | Department Head + Finance notification |
   | Director       | <= $250k                  | Director + Finance + Legal |
   | VP             | <= $1M                    | VP + Finance + Legal |
   | C-level / Board| > $1M                     | CFO + GC + CEO + Board (if > $5M) |
4. Standard clauses & non-negotiables:
- Data residency and security addenda required for Private deployments.
- No change to export controls clause without Legal approval.
- Indemnity cap standard: limited to lesser of fees paid in preceding 12 months or $500k unless approved by GC.

Procurement and vendor onboarding:
1. Thresholds and PO requirements:
   - Purchases < $5k: team may approve via expense workflow; no PO required.
   - $5k - $50k: require PO, Procurement Ops must review vendor, payment terms standard Net30.
   - $50k - $250k: Procurement + Finance approval + vendor risk assessment.
   - > $250k: Procurement + Finance + Legal + Exec approval.
2. Vendor due diligence checklist (required for > $50k or security-sensitive vendors):
   - SOC2 report or equivalent security certification.
   - Data processing agreement (if vendor will handle PII).
   - Proof of insurance and indemnity language.
   - Financial health check (3rd party or internal credit review).
3. Payment terms and exceptions:
   - Standard vendor payment: Net30 from invoice receipt.
   - Preferred payment: ACH. Cards allowed for < $5k with reconciliation.
   - Exceptions: extended payment terms > Net30 require Finance approval and documented business justification.

Revenue recognition (RevRec) policy summary:
- Principle: Recognize revenue when control of promised goods/services transfers to the customer, following ASC 606 five-step model.
- Common Redwood treatments:
  - Usage-based hosted API revenue: recognized ratably as usage occurs (consumed tokens / billing interval).
  - Reserved capacity (Dedicated): if contract includes a non-refundable reservation fee for capacity and no separate performance obligation, recognize over the reservation period ratably unless criteria for upfront recognition apply (consult RevRec team).
  - Private deployments and professional services: separate software license vs services. License revenue recognized on delivery if standalone; professional services recognized over time using input method (percentage of completion) when criteria met.
  - Bundled arrangements: allocate transaction price to performance obligations using relative stand-alone selling prices (SSP).
- Documentation required for RevRec close:
  - Executed contract and order forms.
  - Billing schedule and payment terms.
  - Evidence of delivery/acceptance (for on-prem/private installs and professional services).
- Monthly RevRec close tasks:
  1. Finance collects all signed contracts and order forms.
  2. Billing team verifies invoiced amounts vs contract schedule.
  3. Revenue entries posted to GL with RevRec memo.

Billing operations and accounts receivable (AR):
- Invoicing cadence:
  - Usage invoices: billed monthly in arrears by default; customers may opt for monthly estimated billing with true-up.
  - Annual committed contracts: invoice per term negotiated (annual upfront, quarterly, or monthly).
- Standard payment terms: Net30; late fee policy = 1.5% monthly after 30 days unless otherwise agreed.
- Credit & collections workflow:
  1. Day 0–30: Automated invoice delivery and reminder emails.
  2. Day 31–60: Collections team issues escalation to customer finance and notifies Sales/AE.
  3. Day 61–90: Credit hold triggers (service may be suspended for Hosted API) following Legal & Sales coordination.
  4. >90 days: Legal referral for recovery; provisions for bad debt recorded in monthly close.
- Discounts and credits:
  - All discounts must be approved by Finance and documented in the order form.
  - Credits for service outages follow the SLA credit table in the MSA; product/engineering must provide postmortem and credit calculation to Billing.

Controls, reporting, and audit readiness:
- Required artifacts for internal and external audit:
  - Signed contracts, amendment history, order forms.
  - Billing logs and invoice history.
  - RevRec memos and journal entries with supporting calculations.
- Monthly reports produced by Finance and shared with leadership:
  - MRR/ARR rollforward, churn, bookings vs billings, days sales outstanding (DSO).
  - Revenue by product/route and deferred revenue balance.
- KPIs and targets:
  - DSO target: < 45 days.
  - Billing accuracy target: 99.5% monthly invoice accuracy.
  - RevRec close SLA: complete and posted within 5 business days after month-end.

Escalations and exceptions:
- Contractual exceptions: any deviation from standard clauses requires Legal review and documented risk acceptance.
- Procurement exceptions: sole-source > $50k requires Procurement approval plus written business rationale and Exec sign-off.
- RevRec edge cases: consult RevRec accountant (Finance) for multi-element arrangements, variable consideration >10% of transaction price, or significant financing components.

Appendices & templates:
- Templates included (Finance Drive):
  - Budget template (monthly/quarterly tabs).
  - Forecast workbook (canonical).
  - Standard MSA and Order Form templates.
  - PO request form and vendor onboarding checklist.
  - RevRec memo template and revenue allocation worksheet.

Change log:

- 2025-03-10: Initial published version of integrated playbook.

Notes & best practices:
- Always attach the executed order form to the contract record in the Contract Repository before booking revenue.
- Engage Finance and Legal early in deal cycles for custom commercial terms or long-term committed capacity (>12 months).
- Maintain a single source of truth for forecasts; avoid ad-hoc spreadsheets outside the Finance Drive.

End of document.
